Population.evidence_source: Whereas some decedents took to drinking possibly to water down the psychological distress, others seemed to have imbibed alcohol to ease the distress believed to accompany suicide (Rossow, 2005). In other words, they used alcohol as an energizer in order to accomplish their mission. For example, one deceased accidentally got to know about the HIV status of one of his wives (polygamy is part of the Acholi culture) when he came across a packet of Anti Retro Virus medication and the medical form. He could have instantly perceived himself as having contracted the virus, but because he had the benefit of doubt, he sought confirmation from the wife herself. Upon re-ceiving the confirmation, he "suddenly changed, started drinking recklessly and heavily. He refused to report back to the work place . . ." (case3:informant1). He just buried himself in alcohol, and within that same period planned to end his life. According to Hufford (2001), in vulnerable individuals a state of acute intoxication with alcohol may trigger a suicidal act. This state may increase impulsiveness, suicidal ideation, limit cognitive functions and one's ability to see alternative coping strategies (Hufford, 2001). This could have been the case with the decedent referred to above. First, the traumatization by the two decades of war may have exposed him to a general suicide vulnerability as traumatic life events are known to be associated with suicide risk (Blaauw, Arensman, Kraaij, Winkel, & Bout, 2005). Second, the shock of knowing he could be HIV positive, an illness that is not only debilitating but still socially stigmatized in some communities in Uganda. And third, anticipating the inability to fulfill his duties as a father and a husband when full-blown AIDS develops may have triggered acute emotional pain and suicidal ideation. In response, he impulsively went on a binge, which initially could have been seen as a way of concealing the felt emotional pain at the time, but in the process of getting intoxicated suicide may have been triggered and his judgment constricted. For another deceased, ever since he received reports that his son had died in captivity, he apparently resolved to end his life but may not have had courage until he decided to go on a drinking spree as indicated below:Whenever he got drunk he could talk about that [committing suicide] and sometimes he cried, saying that one day he will follow his son plus his brothers, no future for him. Some days he could talk the whole night. I could try to console him but he remained sad all the time. This went on and on. So one day he decided to disappear from home. I received reports from people that he was in drinking joints drinking his head off. He spent two complete days without eating and just drinking. (case5:informant3)In the first part of the quote the informant seemed to imply that the decedent had already made up his mind to end his life. According to Rossow (2005), some people intoxicate themselves to get up the courage to fulfill their suicidal plan and/or to reduce their pain, consciousness, or fear. Motivation for alcohol consumption among suicide completers is a way of helping them to effect their suicidal ideation (Rossow, 2005). The two days of binge drinking without food in our example can be seen in this light.
